name: Phishing
instructions: Does this email look like phishing or a scam? Signs: asks to log in, verify an account or pay via a link; sender name does not match the address domain; threats of account suspension or legal action; unexpected attachments or prize claims.

name: Spam
instructions: Is this unsolicited bulk email the recipient never signed up for? Newsletters and promotions from services the recipient actually uses are NOT spam.

name: Category
instructions: Which category fits this email best?

items.d: Written by a friend, family member or acquaintance about private life
About the recipient's job: colleagues, projects, teaching duties, contracts, timesheets
About the recipient's own studies: courses, exams, grades, enrollment, university administration
Recurring editorial content, digests or news the recipient subscribed to
Promotions, offers, discounts or marketing from a company
Orders, shipping, invoices, receipts, payments, refunds, subscriptions
Automated service notices: security alerts, login codes, password resets, account changes, GitHub/CI, social media
Fits none of the above

name: Sender
instructions: Who is the email mainly from, from the recipient's point of view?

items.d: Someone at the recipient's workplace without authority over them
Someone the recipient reports to or who assigns their work
Lecturers, examination office, student services, HR or other institutional staff
Another student, e.g. course or group-work partner
Someone from the recipient's private life
A person outside the recipient's organization writing personally (client, partner, landlord)
A company or organization, including its support staff, newsletters and marketing
Machine-generated with no human author (noreply, alerts, receipts, CI, codes)
Cannot be determined

name: Recipient role
instructions: What is the recipient's role in this email?

items.d: Written specifically to the recipient, one-to-one
Sent to a small group or team; the recipient is expected to take part
The recipient is only kept informed (e.g. CC); others are expected to act
Mailing list, newsletter or broadcast to many people

name: Relevance
instructions: How relevant is this email to the recipient personally?

items.d: Nothing to do with the recipient's life, work, studies or interests
Loosely related; safe to skip
Might be worth a quick look
The recipient will want to read it
Directly concerns the recipient personally

name: Action needed?
instructions: Does the email ask or clearly expect the recipient personally to do something (reply, decide, pay, attend, complete a task)? Generic marketing calls-to-action like 'Shop now' or 'Read more' do not count.

name: Primary action
instructions: What is the main thing the recipient has to do?

items.d: Answer a question or confirm something
Read and give feedback on a document, code or proposal
Make a choice or give approval
Do work outside email: prepare, fix, submit, register
Pay an invoice, fee or outstanding amount
Attend or respond to a meeting or event invitation
Pass the information on to someone else
Use a code or confirmation link, or check an account
Read only / FYI

name: Attention
instructions: Today is {{weekday}}, {{today}}; the email was received {{received}}. By when does the recipient need to read or act on this email at the latest?

items.d: Within about an hour, e.g. a login code, a meeting starting soon, an ongoing incident
No time pressure
The deadline or event has passed, or the code/link has expired

name: Importance
instructions: Regardless of timing: how bad would it be if the recipient never dealt with this email?

items.d: Nothing happens
Small inconvenience or a missed nice-to-have
Noticeable consequences, e.g. an annoyed colleague, a small fee, a missed opportunity
Significant consequences for work, studies, money or relationships
Serious harm: lost money, failed exam or contract, security breach, safety risk

name: Urgency driver
instructions: What is the main reason this email needs attention?

items.d: A date by which something must be done
Payments, charges, refunds, fees
Suspicious login, password, account access
Risk to someone's health or safety
A person is blocked or waiting on the recipient
Legal, contractual, academic or administrative requirement
Another reason
The email does not need attention

name: Reply effort
instructions: If the recipient should reply, how much effort will the reply take?

items.d: A one-liner, under 2 minutes
A few sentences, about 5-10 minutes
Requires thought, looking things up or checking with others
Needs research, coordination or a meeting first

name: Follow-up
instructions: Is this a reminder, follow-up or escalation of an earlier message (e.g. 'gentle reminder', 'second notice', 'still waiting for')?

name: Calendar
instructions: Does the email contain a meeting, appointment or event with a specific date and time that the recipient might add to a calendar? A deadline alone does not count.

name: Event type
instructions: If the email is about a calendar event, what kind of update is it?

items.d: A new meeting, appointment or event is proposed
An existing plan or booking is confirmed
Time, place or details of a known event changed
An event is cancelled
Reminder of an already known event

name: Transaction type
instructions: If the email is about a purchase or payment, what stage is it?

items.d: Dispatch, tracking, delivery or pickup notice
Proof of a completed payment or a bill
Payment request, overdue notice, dunning
Renewal, trial ending, price change, cancellation

name: One-time code
instructions: Does the email contain a one-time code, a verification or magic-login link, or a password-reset link?
